column1: # docs/pointer-groundtruth-I-II.tsv — THE HELD-OUT LABELLED GROUND TRUTH for the bare-pointer class.
# WHAT THIS IS. Every `<token> in <target>` construction in paper-I.md and paper-II.md at revision
# 83db4d5 whose TARGET is BARE under wt160's named-target tests N1-N6 — 88 rows, of 125
# constructions in all (44 here from Paper I, 44 from Paper II). It is the SISTER FILE to
# docs/pointer-groundtruth.tsv, which holds the same thing for Papers III and IV at 07cd47e, and it
# exists for one reason: PAPERS I AND II ARE HELD-OUT TEXT. Nothing in wt160's N1-N6, in wt166's
# DOC_NOUNS or CLAIM_NOUNS, in any verb list this programme has used, or in the candidate tests
# T1-T6 was written against a single sentence of them.
# WHY IT EXISTS. REVIEW-029 measured two numbers on the corpus they were built against and could
# not do otherwise without contaminating it: T5's recall of 1.0000 (the document-noun test, whose
# noun list was written by the session that had just read the labels) and T6's failure (a test
# invented AFTER reading those labels). Its section 8 falsifiers 4 and 5 name running them on
# held-out text as the outstanding work. These are the held-out labels. See REVIEW-030.
# HOW IT WAS BUILT. All 88 rows were READ, in context, by wealthTensor-90, and labelled by
# REVIEW-028 section 3's rule, fixed before this reading and unchanged:
#   POINTER iff (a) the construction asserts that some content is LOCATED IN a document,
#   artefact, run or record — the reader is being asked to go there to check — AND (b) the
#   target as written carries no handle a reader could follow.
# Clause (b) holds for all 88 by construction, since N1-N6 are silent on every row. So the
# labelling decides clause (a) alone, 88 times. No verb list, no DOC_NOUNS, no CLAIM_NOUNS and no
# candidate test's OUTPUT was consulted while labelling.
# DISCLOSED CONTAMINATION, because the honest version of "held-out" has to say what the labeller
# had already read. wealthTensor-90 read scripts/wt166_pointer_groundtruth.py in full — including
# the DOC_NOUNS list — while orienting, BEFORE labelling. The labels were made from the rule and
# the sentences, and no row was checked against DOC_NOUNS at labelling time; but the labeller was
# not ignorant of the list and this file will not pretend otherwise. REVIEW-030 section 8
# falsifier 1 states the attack this leaves open and how to run it. The protocol repair — read the
# corpus BEFORE the instrument — is carded for the next held-out exercise.
# COLUMNS.  file · line · token · target · label · confidence · reason
#   (file, line, token, target) is the KEY. It is unique across all 88 rows and every component is
#   recomputed from 83db4d5, so the labels cannot drift from the corpus: wt169 REFUSES (exit 2) if
#   the recomputed key set differs from this file's by a single row.
#   `line` is the source line of the FLATTENED text's match, as wt160 reports it.
#   `confidence` is FIRM or SOFT, and is not decoration: wt169 scores every candidate THREE times —
#   against the labels as written (PRIMARY, 7 pointers), against FIRM pointers only (STRICT, 4),
#   and against PRIMARY plus every SOFT NOT-POINTER (LOOSE, 16) — so no verdict in REVIEW-030 rests
#   on a judgement call. There are 9 SOFT NOT-POINTER rows.
# THE SEVEN. Four are FIRM: `I 35 Fixed in the code and the tests`, `I 460 and in the test`,
# `II 11 named in the data-availability statement` (the same construction Paper III carries, and
# the only one of the seven whose target holds a DOC_NOUNS word), and
# `II 132 precision in the implementation`. Three are SOFT: `I 95 elsewhere in this programme`,
# `I 319 asserted in the test suite`, `II 177 visible in the third column`.
# THESE MANUSCRIPTS ARE OUT OF SCOPE FOR REPAIR. wealthTensor-90's at-bat is to MEASURE, and a
# repair pass on Papers I and II is a different piece of work with a different risk profile. The
# seven are REPORTED in REVIEW-030 section 5.1 and carded; not one word of either manuscript was
# changed by the session that wrote this file. The labels are pinned to 83db4d5 and do not move
# when a later session repairs them.
